name: Ctrl+C
description: Interrupts a running operation. If nothing is running, the first press clears the prompt input and a second press exits Claude Code
when_to_use: Interrupts a running operation.

conditions: Interrupts a running operation. If nothing is running, the first press clears the prompt input and a second press exits Claude Code

name: Ctrl+X Ctrl+K
display_name: Stop all running background subagents in this session, and turn off artifact auto-replies for the rest of it. Press twice within 3 seconds to confirm
role: Stop all running background subagents in this session, and turn off artifact auto-replies for the rest of it. Press twice within 3 seconds to confirm
description: Subagent control

name: Ctrl+D
description: The first press shows a confirmation hint and a second press within 800ms exits. When the prompt has text, Ctrl+D deletes the character after the cursor instead
when_to_use: The first press shows a confirmation hint and a second press within 800ms exits.

conditions: The first press shows a confirmation hint and a second press within 800ms exits. When the prompt has text, Ctrl+D deletes the character after the cursor instead

name: Ctrl+G / Ctrl+X Ctrl+E
description: Edit your prompt or custom response in your default text editor. Ctrl+X Ctrl+E is the readline-native binding. Turn on Show last response in external editor in /config to prepend Claude's previous reply as #-commented context above your prompt; Claude Code strips the comment block when you save
when_to_use: Edit your prompt or custom response in your default text editor.

conditions: Edit your prompt or custom response in your default text editor. Ctrl+X Ctrl+E is the readline-native binding. name: Ctrl+L
description: Forces a full terminal redraw, keeping input and conversation history. Use this to recover if the display becomes garbled or partially blank
when_to_use: Forces a full terminal redraw, keeping input and conversation history.

conditions: Forces a full terminal redraw, keeping input and conversation history. Use this to recover if the display becomes garbled or partially blank

name: Ctrl+O
description: Shows detailed tool usage and execution, with a timestamp and the model used on each assistant message. Also expands lines that collapse by default, such as MCP calls, shown as a single Called slack 3 times line, and messages from your other sessions, shown as a one-line Message from @<sender> preview
when_to_use: Shows detailed tool usage and execution, with a timestamp and the model used on each assistant message.

name: Ctrl+R
description: Search through previous commands interactively
when_to_use: Search through previous commands interactively.

name: Ctrl+V / Cmd+V
description: Inserts an [Image #N] chip at the cursor so you can reference it positionally in your prompt. On WSL, both Ctrl+V and Alt+V are bound; use Alt+V if your terminal intercepts Ctrl+V
when_to_use: Inserts an [Image #N] chip at the cursor so you can reference it positionally in your prompt.

conditions: Inserts an [Image #N] chip at the cursor so you can reference it positionally in your prompt. On WSL, both Ctrl+V and Alt+V are bound; use Alt+V if your terminal intercepts Ctrl+V

name: Ctrl+B
description: Backgrounds Bash commands and agents. Tmux users press twice
when_to_use: Backgrounds Bash commands and agents.

name: Ctrl+T
description: Show or hide Claude's to-do checklist in the status area. This is not the background-task view; use /tasks to see running shells and subagents
when_to_use: Show or hide Claude's to-do checklist in the status area.

name: Ctrl+S
description: With text in the input, stashes it and clears the prompt. Pressed again on an empty prompt, restores the stashed text, cursor position, and pasted content
when_to_use: With text in the input, stashes it and clears the prompt.

name: Tab
display_name: Accept an autocomplete suggestion, or add a comment to a permission answer
role: Accept an autocomplete suggestion, or add a comment to a permission answer

name: Up/Down arrows / Ctrl+P
display_name: Move cursor or navigate command history
role: Move cursor or navigate command history
description: When the input spans more than one visual row, whether wrapped or multiline, first moves the cursor within the prompt. Once the cursor is on the first or last visual row, pressing again navigates command history. While you have messages queued, Up from the first row instead takes them back

name: Esc
display_name: Interrupt Claude, or close a dialog
role: Interrupt Claude, or close a dialog
description: Stop the current response or tool call mid-turn so you can redirect. Claude keeps the work done so far. If you have messages queued, Claude Code sends them next. When a dialog is open, Esc closes the dialog. On a permission prompt, Esc declines the action, the same as No without a comment

examples.explanation: Interrupt Claude, or close a dialog.

when_to_use: Stop the current response or tool call mid-turn so you can redirect.

conditions: Stop the current response or tool call mid-turn so you can redirect. Claude keeps the work done so far. If you have messages queued, Claude Code sends them next. name: Esc Esc
description: When the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it and saves the draft to history so Up recalls it. When the input is empty, double Esc opens the rewind menu to restore or summarize code and conversation from a previous point
when_to_use: When the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it and saves the draft to history so Up recalls it.

conditions: When the prompt input contains text, double Esc clears it and saves the draft to history so Up recalls it. When the input is empty, double Esc opens the rewind menu to restore or summarize code and conversation from a previous point

name: Shift+Tab
description: Cycle through default (labeled Manual in the mode indicator), acceptEdits, plan, and, when available, bypassPermissions and then auto. From auto, the first press switches to default. See permission modes. On a file permission prompt, the same key closes an open comment field. With no field open, it selects the option that allows the action for the rest of the session, when the prompt offers that option
when_to_use: Cycle through default (labeled Manual in the mode indicator), acceptEdits, plan, and, when available, bypassPermissions and then auto.
